recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-12501 unless a future ballot decision changes the Provenance.authorization/why split or the Provenance.activity datatype.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive Security WG issue requested changing Provenance.reason and Provenance.activity back to CodeableConcept rather than Coding because Provenance activity/reason concepts may need multiple coding systems and translations.
initial_application: The historical application appears in commit 84f8086d21facb3551bfb28481156250510ae48b, whose message lists Provenance GF#12501 and whose provenance spreadsheet patch changed both Provenance.reason and Provenance.activity from Coding to CodeableConcept.
additional_context: FHIR-9105 was the earlier Published issue that changed Provenance.activity and Provenance.reason from CodeableConcept to Coding, creating the state FHIR-12501 reversed. A later current-source change, FHIR-54833, explains that old Provenance.reason is now represented by Provenance.authorization for coded authorization/purpose-of-use and Provenance.why for free text; that later issue explicitly dropped authorization back to CodeableConcept. source/fhir.ini confirms Provenance is active and aliases Provenance.reason to Provenance.authorization.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because source/provenance/structuredefinition-Provenance.xml currently defines Provenance.authorization and Provenance.activity with CodeableConcept, and no relevant Coding datatype remains on those Provenance definitions.
